zeugmamosaic.name: Zeugma Mosaic Museum
zeugmamosaic.slogan: Roman floors rescued from a river that rose to drown them.
zeugmamosaic.line: Opened in 2011, it shows mosaics saved when the Birecik Dam flooded the Roman city of Zeugma.

gaziantepkalesi.name: Gaziantep Castle
gaziantepkalesi.slogan: A round Roman fortress on a hill, with a city wrapped around it.
gaziantepkalesi.line: Hittites used the hill as a lookout, Romans built the castle, and Justinian enlarged it between AD 527 and 565.

rumkale.name: Rumkale
rumkale.slogan: A fortress on a rock where the Euphrates curls around its feet.
rumkale.line: From 1203 to 1293 this clifftop fortress was the seat of the Armenian Catholicos, head of the Armenian Church.

gulluoglu.name: Güllüoğlu Baklava
gulluoglu.slogan: Pistachio and paper-thin pastry, the Antep way.
gulluoglu.line: In 2013, Gaziantep baklava became the first Turkish product to win EU protected geographical indication status.

zeugmaantikkent.name: Zeugma Ancient City
zeugmaantikkent.slogan: A Roman crossing on the Euphrates, half of it still underwater.
zeugmaantikkent.line: Founded around 300 BC by Seleucus I, Zeugma is named for its bridge of boats across the Euphrates.
